items.title: Catherine Russell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 26, 2018
items.q: So we were sitting at the feet of Leontyne Price. And she said, “Hello” you know

ctx.x: So the idea of being in front of an audience was, you got that at an early age and got fairly comfortable with it? © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

I would say pre-pubescent life I was very comfortable in front of an audience. I didn’t think about it. I just remember being at the Metropolitan Opera House because when we did “Aida,” which was what I did with the Katherine Dunham Dance Company, we did that for four seasons from 1963 to 1967. So we were at the old Metropolitan Opera House for two seasons. They tore that down, they built Lincoln Center then we moved in to the new Metropolitan Opera House for two seasons. So I think we were at the old Met. And it…
The innocence of youth, right? Like you didn’t know that this should be nerve wracking.
